notes:
Account summary
- Regulated healthcare provider network + patient engagement apps. Evaluating Redwood for Private deployment (VPC) due to PHI handling and strict data residency requirements.
- They want multi-region availability but with hard boundaries: failover must not violate residency (no cross-border) and must be auditable.

Current stage
- Evaluation. They are comparing options (Azure OpenAI in locked-down tenant, Bedrock, and "self-host open models"). Redwood is in for Private because they want routing/observability + cost levers without building a full serving stack.

Workloads / use cases (stated)
- Patient portal assistant (chat): appointment/benefits Q&A with retrieval; must be stable under traffic spikes.
- Clinical note summarization (batch + near-real-time): throughput heavy, cost sensitive; needs quality monitoring.
- Internal doc search for care teams (embeddings + reranking).

Key requirements (technical)
- Deployment: Redwood Private in Northstar-owned cloud VPC. Prefer AWS but not committed.
- Data residency: PHI must remain in the US. Explicitly: no automatic failover to non-US regions. They also have internal policy language about "state-level residency" for a subset of lines of business; they are verifying whether that applies to this program.
- Failover boundaries:
  - They want HA within allowed geography only.
  - They are open to active/active across two US regions IF both are pre-approved and if routing decisions are logged.
  - Quote from security lead: "We can’t have the system silently deciding to ship PHI somewhere else during an incident." (applies to cross-border; they’re still debating cross-US-region.)
- Observability: want dashboards for availability/latency by region + clear indication of failover state. They asked for a "single pane" view for incident bridges.
- Auditability: need an audit trail of automation decisions (who/what/why/when) and retention aligned to their internal incident review policy.
- Security controls:
  - SSO/SAML for Console access; role-based access control (least privilege).
  - KMS integration (customer-managed keys) for any at-rest encryption Redwood controls.
  - Retention controls: request/response logging defaults must be configurable; PHI must not be stored by default.
  - Network: prefer private connectivity; egress allowlists and explicit ports.

Reliability / failover discussion (important)
- They are concerned about what happens during a regional impairment:
  - Hosted-style cross-region automation is attractive operationally, but they need deterministic policy evaluation and guardrails.
  - For Private, they want a documented recommended pattern: "strict residency mode" (no cross-region failover; degrade gracefully) vs "approved multi-region" (failover only between approved US regions).
- Asked whether automated failover requires manual approval:
  - Northstar’s current leaning: for production, keep automation in dry-run / advisory initially, then move to automatic only after 1–2 game day-style tests and once compliance signs off.

Open questions
- Does Northstar allow automatic failover from us-east -> us-west under the same PHI policy, or do they require on-call approval (human-in-the-loop)?
- Do they require per-tenant isolation for patient portal vs internal workloads? (Could drive dedicated pools within Private.)
- What audit event fields do they require in the export (tenant, route, model, trigger reason, evidence signals, rollback reason)?

Next steps (tactical)
- Schedule: joint architecture + security review (Northstar platform + security + Redwood Private deployments).
- Redwood (Simran Kaur + Dev Patel) to send:
  - Proposed failover boundary matrix for Private (allowed/blocked scenarios) and recommended guardrails.
  - Example audit event schema excerpt + retention/forwarding options.
  - Guidance on "game day" approach for Private (staging-first, limited blast radius) and what success criteria we recommend.

Internal Redwood notes
- This account is sensitive to any suggestion of cross-border routing. Use precise language: "approved region set" + "policy-enforced" + "audited decisions".
- Keep reliability messaging consistent with our current failover automation upgrade work (signals hierarchy, rollback guardrails, deterministic evaluation). Avoid promising fully bespoke automation for Private; position as supported patterns + tooling.
- Support requested by customer: they asked for an example response to: "How do you define multi-region availability?" (tie to SLO definition but don’t overcommit to external reporting).
